title: Reviews and reports
purpose: When a meeting, a client or an investor is waiting on numbers, open Reviews and reports to know what happened, why, and what to say, in minutes, with numbers that hold up.
fires: The Sunday night spreadsheet, the monthly slide deck built by hand, the agency's report on its own work, and the tab-by-tab check of every platform.
not_for: A founder who wants to watch today's ad spend live, or an accountant closing the books; this is for reading and telling what happened, not for bookkeeping.

jobs.job: When it is Sunday night and the Monday meeting is at 9, tell me what happened last week, why, and the 3 calls I need to make, so I walk in ready instead of up late in 6 tabs
jobs.circumstance: Sunday, 10pm, Shopify, Meta, Klaviyo and the bank open in tabs, a partner and the team expecting a plan at 9

progress.functional: the week on one page: what moved, the likely cause, and the calls ranked
progress.emotional: get Sunday night back; stop the dread of missing something
progress.social: lead the Monday meeting with answers, not a screen share of tabs

jobs.hire_today: the founder's own spreadsheet, about 90 minutes every Sunday; or an ops hire who builds it
jobs.fire: the Sunday spreadsheet and the tour of 6 tabs

forces.push: every Sunday is lost and problems still slip past
forces.pull: one page ready Sunday evening, with the 3 calls ranked by money at stake
forces.habit: I only trust numbers I pulled myself
forces.anxiety: what if the page misses the one thing I would have spotted

jobs.little_hire: every Sunday night or Monday before 9

watch.metric: minutes the founder spends preparing the weekly meeting, and decisions logged from it, weekly

drives.metric: days from a key number leaving its normal range to a logged decision

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 90 minutes on Sunday night, 0 decisions written down. After: 10 minutes, 3 decisions logged by 10am Monday.
jobs.not_for: a founder who runs no weekly meeting and checks the store daily by feel, with sales under a few thousand a month

jobs.job: When the week's sales look good, tell me the profit left after product cost, shipping, discounts, returns and ads, so I do not celebrate a week that lost money
jobs.circumstance: Monday, sales are up 22 percent on a promo week, the team is pleased, the founder has a bad feeling about the discount depth

progress.functional: profit after all costs for the week, next to sales
progress.emotional: stop the gap between a good-looking week and the bank balance
progress.social: tell a partner the real result, not the flattering one

jobs.hire_today: the bookkeeper's profit and loss, 3 to 6 weeks late; weekly, nothing, because the costs sit in 5 systems
jobs.fire: judging the week on sales and ROAS alone

forces.push: past promo weeks looked great and lost money
forces.pull: profit after ads for the week, on the same page as sales
forces.habit: sales is the number the whole team watches
forces.anxiety: what if the cost data is wrong and the profit number misleads

jobs.little_hire: weekly, and the day after any promo ends

watch.metric: profit after product cost, shipping, discounts, returns and ad spend, weekly
watch.source: store orders, ad accounts and product cost in the brand brain

drives.metric: contribution margin, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a $60,000 sales week turned out to lose $3,000 after ads. After: seen on Monday, the promo depth cut from 30 to 20 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store with no product costs on file; it must enter them first or the number shows unavailable

jobs.job: When I have 1 hour and 8 brands, show me which 2 need me this week and why, so I spend the hour where a client is about to slip
jobs.circumstance: agency owner, Monday 8am, 8 client brands, 1 hour before back-to-back calls, account managers each say their client is fine

progress.functional: brands ranked by what needs attention, with the reason for each
progress.emotional: stop the fear that a client is quietly failing
progress.social: call the client before the client calls, and back up the account manager

jobs.hire_today: account managers' status updates in a weekly call; the owner checking brand dashboards tab by tab
jobs.fire: the round-robin status call and the tab-by-tab check

forces.push: clients leave after problems nobody raised
forces.pull: one page of all brands, worst first, with the number and the cause
forces.habit: trust the account managers to raise issues
forces.anxiety: what if a brand that looks fine on paper is about to churn for other reasons

jobs.little_hire: every Monday, and when any brand's key number jumps

watch.metric: brands with a key number outside its normal range for 2 or more weeks, and days until someone acted

drives.metric: client retention, brands kept per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the owner found a brand's 30 percent drop in week 4 through the client's angry email. After: flagged in week 1, fixed by week 2.
jobs.not_for: a founder running 1 brand; this is for someone running many

jobs.job: When a client emails 'how did this month go?', send a clear answer with the numbers, the reasons and next month's plan, so they stay and stop worrying
jobs.circumstance: agency account manager, the 3rd of the month, the client is unhappy about flat sales, the report takes a full day to build

progress.functional: month numbers, what caused them and the plan, in words the client reads
progress.emotional: stop dreading the client call
progress.social: look in control and honest to the client

jobs.hire_today: the account manager building slides by hand from 4 platforms; a reporting tool that dumps charts
jobs.fire: the monthly slide build and the chart-dump report

forces.push: a day a month per client lost; clients cannot read meaning in charts
forces.pull: a report the client understands in 3 minutes, ready on the 2nd
forces.habit: our slide template has always been fine
forces.anxiety: what if the numbers differ from what the client sees in Shopify

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and whenever a client asks

watch.metric: days from month end to report sent, per client, and client replies asking 'why'

drives.metric: client retention, months kept

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: reports go out on day 6 and take 7 hours each. After: day 2, 45 minutes to check and send.
jobs.not_for: a founder with no client or partner to report to

jobs.job: When a number drops, tell me the likely cause, like stock, price, an ad, a site change or the season, so I fix the cause and not the symptom
jobs.circumstance: Wednesday, conversion is down 18 percent week on week, the team guesses at 4 different causes

progress.functional: the likely cause with the evidence, and what to check next
progress.emotional: stop the helpless feeling of a line going down
progress.social: point the right person at the fix instead of blaming the wrong team

jobs.hire_today: an analyst or the agency's guess; the founder's gut
jobs.fire: guessing in a group chat

forces.push: each wrong guess costs a week
forces.pull: the cause named with the numbers that show it
forces.habit: we raise ad spend when sales drop
forces.anxiety: what if the named cause is wrong and we fix the wrong thing

jobs.little_hire: any time a key number moves more than its normal range

watch.metric: share of top movers each week with a named cause and the evidence

drives.metric: days from a drop to a fix going live

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 3 week drop was blamed on ads; it was a sold-out size. After: cause named on day 2.
jobs.not_for: a store with only a few orders a week, where most moves are noise

jobs.job: When the agency or Meta says it drove $80,000 in sales, set it next to the orders the store actually got, so I move money on real numbers
jobs.circumstance: month end, the agency's report shows ROAS of 4, the store's sales rose 5 percent

progress.functional: claimed orders next to real store orders from that channel, same window
progress.emotional: stop feeling that I am being sold a story
progress.social: challenge the agency or the platform with facts

jobs.hire_today: nothing; most founders read the platform's number as truth because checking needs an analyst
jobs.fire: the agency's report as the source of truth

forces.push: budget moves on numbers that may be double counted
forces.pull: claimed versus actual, side by side, with the gap named
forces.habit: the platform says so
forces.anxiety: what if our own tracking is the one that is wrong

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and before any budget increase

watch.metric: gap between orders a platform or agency claims and store orders from that channel, same window

drives.metric: blended cost per new customer, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the platform claims 1,200 orders; the store shows 700 new orders in total. After: budget set on the 700.
jobs.not_for: a store with no paid ads and no agency

jobs.job: When the investor update is due tomorrow, give me a first draft from real numbers with what went well, what did not and what we need, so I send it on time and it matches the books
jobs.circumstance: Thursday evening, the quarterly update is due Friday, the last one went out 3 weeks late

progress.functional: a draft with the quarter's numbers, the story and the asks
progress.emotional: stop the dread that comes every quarter
progress.social: look steady and honest to investors

jobs.hire_today: the founder alone for a day, or a fractional CFO at an hourly rate
jobs.fire: a blank page and a day of pulling numbers

forces.push: late or rosy updates cost investor trust
forces.pull: a draft built from the same numbers the team uses every week
forces.habit: I write it myself because it is my voice
forces.anxiety: what if an investor spots a number that does not match last quarter

jobs.little_hire: quarterly, and before any board meeting or fundraise

watch.metric: days from quarter end to update sent

drives.metric: investor follow-up questions about numbers, per update

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: sent 21 days after quarter end with 2 corrections. After: sent in 5 days, 0 corrections.
jobs.not_for: a founder with no investors or lenders

jobs.job: When Shopify, GA4 and the agency show 3 different sales numbers, give one agreed number for each and say where it comes from, so the meeting argues about decisions, not data
jobs.circumstance: the weekly meeting starts with 20 minutes on whose number is right

progress.functional: one number per metric with its source and window written down
progress.emotional: end the frustration of the same argument every week
progress.social: stop looking unsure of my own numbers in front of the team

jobs.hire_today: an analyst who reconciles by hand, or nothing
jobs.fire: each person bringing their own number

forces.push: meetings stall on data fights
forces.pull: one agreed source per number, shown on the page
forces.habit: everyone trusts their own tool
forces.anxiety: what if the chosen source is the wrong one

jobs.little_hire: weekly, and whenever a new tool is added

watch.metric: report numbers with a missing or conflicting source

drives.metric: minutes of each weekly meeting spent on data disputes

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 20 minutes a meeting on whose number is right. After: 0; one sales number from store orders.
jobs.not_for: a founder working alone with a single tool

jobs.job: When profit is up but the bank balance is down, show sales, profit and cash side by side, so I know why before I tell my partner we are fine
jobs.circumstance: month end, profit and loss shows a good month, the bank has $20,000 less than last month, a stock order is due

progress.functional: sales, profit and cash as 3 separate lines with what moved each
progress.emotional: stop the knot in the stomach when the bank does not match the report
progress.social: give a partner an honest picture

jobs.hire_today: the bookkeeper or accountant, monthly and late
jobs.fire: reading profit as if it were cash

forces.push: cash surprises before stock orders
forces.pull: 3 numbers side by side with the stock bought named
forces.habit: profit is the headline
forces.anxiety: what if the cash forecast is wrong

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and before any large stock order

watch.metric: cash on hand at week end versus the lowest point in the 13 week forecast

drives.metric: cash runway, weeks

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a profitable month left $8,000 in the bank. After: seen 3 weeks earlier, stock order split in 2.
jobs.not_for: a store with no bank or accounting link; the cash line shows unavailable

jobs.job: When a key number has been off for 2 weeks running, flag it before it becomes a month, so I act while it is small
jobs.circumstance: repeat rate has slipped 2 weeks in a row; nobody has said anything

progress.functional: a flag when a number sits outside its normal range 2 weeks running
progress.emotional: trust that drift will not go unseen
progress.social: raise it with the team early

jobs.hire_today: nothing; one bad week is ignored and nobody watches the second
jobs.fire: waiting for the month end report

forces.push: problems grow for weeks before they are seen
forces.pull: a short list of numbers out of range, with weeks running
forces.habit: one bad week is noise
forces.anxiety: what if the flags become noise too

watch.metric: key numbers outside their normal range for 2 or more weeks

drives.metric: days from drift starting to a logged decision

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: a 3 week slide in repeat rate found at month end. After: flagged in week 2.
jobs.not_for: a store with under 8 weeks of history; there is no normal range yet

jobs.job: When a quarter is half over, tell me which goals are behind the pace needed, so I change course with weeks left, not days
jobs.circumstance: week 6 of 13, the goal was 1,500 new customers, the team feels busy

progress.functional: each goal against the pace needed to hit it
progress.emotional: stop the end of quarter shock
progress.social: show the team and investors I see it early

jobs.hire_today: the founder's gut, or a quarterly review that comes too late
jobs.fire: finding out at quarter end

forces.push: missed goals with no warning
forces.pull: goals shown with the pace line each week
forces.habit: we check at quarter end
forces.anxiety: what if the goal itself was wrong

watch.metric: progress on each quarterly goal versus the pace needed to hit it

drives.metric: goals hit per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1,500 new customers goal missed by 40 percent, seen in week 13. After: gap seen in week 5, budget moved.
jobs.not_for: a founder with no written quarterly goals

jobs.job: When the month closes, show which changes we made and what each one moved, so I know if the team and the fees are worth it
jobs.circumstance: month end, the agency invoice is $12,000, the report lists numbers but not the work behind them

progress.functional: each change tied to what it moved
progress.emotional: stop wondering what I am paying for
progress.social: hold the team and agency to results

jobs.hire_today: the agency's self-report
jobs.fire: numbers with no link to the work

forces.push: fees rise, results unclear
forces.pull: the month's changes and what each earned
forces.habit: the agency reports on itself
forces.anxiety: what if a change's effect is hard to separate

watch.metric: gross profit banked from changes rolled out this month

drives.metric: gross profit per dollar of agency and team fees, per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $12,000 fee, 0 changes tied to results. After: 4 changes listed, 2 with measured gains worth $18,000.
jobs.not_for: a founder doing all the work alone

jobs.job: When the Black Friday week or another big sale ends, tell me what it really made after discounts, returns and ads, next to last year, so next year's plan starts from truth
jobs.circumstance: first Monday of December, the team celebrates record sales, returns are still coming in

progress.functional: true profit from the sale with returns counted, next to last year
progress.emotional: know if the big week was worth the stress
progress.social: plan next year with the team on the same facts

jobs.hire_today: a bookkeeper's view in January, or nothing
jobs.fire: the record sales headline

forces.push: the same loss-making sale is planned every year
forces.pull: profit after returns for the sale window, with last year beside it
forces.habit: big sales are always worth it
forces.anxiety: what if returns take 60 days to settle

jobs.little_hire: after each big sale, and 45 days later

watch.metric: profit after discounts, returns and ad spend for the sale window, versus the same window last year
watch.source: store orders, returns and ad platforms

drives.metric: contribution margin, quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 'record' Black Friday made $4,000 less profit than last year. After: seen in 45 days, depth changed for next year.
jobs.not_for: a store that runs no big sales

jobs.job: When an account manager looks stretched, show me their booked hours across every brand, so I move work before they drop a client
jobs.circumstance: agency owner, an account manager on 5 brands missed 2 deadlines this week

progress.functional: hours booked per person across brands
progress.emotional: stop fearing the burnout exit
progress.social: protect the team and the clients

jobs.hire_today: asking the account manager, who always says fine; gut
jobs.fire: finding overload when a client complains

forces.push: one overloaded person can lose 2 clients
forces.pull: booked hours per person, flagged over 100 percent
forces.habit: everyone says they are fine
forces.anxiety: what if the hours estimates are wrong

watch.metric: people booked over 100 percent of their available hours this week

drives.metric: client churn per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 2 people at 130 percent, found after a client left. After: flagged, 1 brand moved.
jobs.not_for: a founder with no team

jobs.job: When the month closes, rank products by the profit they made after discounts, shipping and returns, so ads and stock follow profit, not sales
jobs.circumstance: the best seller by sales turns out to be the most returned

progress.functional: profit per product after all costs
progress.emotional: stop backing the wrong product
progress.social: give the buyer and the ads team one list

jobs.hire_today: nothing, or a bookkeeper once a year; product-level costs are hard to pull
jobs.fire: the best sellers list by revenue

forces.push: ads and stock go to products that lose money
forces.pull: a product list by profit
forces.habit: revenue ranks are the norm
forces.anxiety: what if product costs are out of date

watch.metric: gross profit per product after discounts and returns, monthly
watch.source: store orders, returns and product cost

drives.metric: gross margin, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: the #1 seller by sales is #9 by profit. After: its ad budget cut 30 percent.
jobs.not_for: a store with 1 product

jobs.job: When my week is full of standing meetings and reports, show which ones never lead to a decision, so I cut them and get hours back
jobs.circumstance: the founder has 9 standing meetings and 6 weekly reports; most end with 'let's check next week'

progress.functional: each meeting and report with its decisions over 30 days
progress.emotional: relief from a calendar that runs me
progress.social: cut meetings without offending the team

jobs.hire_today: nothing; nobody audits meetings
jobs.fire: the standing calendar

forces.push: hours lost each week
forces.pull: a list of meetings and reports with 0 decisions
forces.habit: meetings feel like work
forces.anxiety: what if cutting a meeting hides a problem

watch.metric: recurring reports not opened in 30 days, and founder hours in standing meetings per week

drives.metric: decisions logged per founder hour in meetings

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 11 hours a week in standing meetings. After: 5 hours, same number of decisions.
jobs.not_for: a founder with fewer than 3 standing meetings

jobs.job: When next month's budget is being set and every channel owner wants more, show where the next dollar earned the most last month, so I split the budget on results, not on who asked
jobs.circumstance: the last Friday of the month, the Meta buyer, the Google freelancer and the email agency each ask for more

progress.functional: each channel's return on its last dollar, not its average
progress.emotional: stop feeling the split is a guess
progress.social: decide fairly between channel owners

jobs.hire_today: the founder's gut, or the agency that runs the biggest channel
jobs.fire: the split by who asks loudest

forces.push: money keeps going to the channel with the best story
forces.pull: each channel's next-dollar return side by side
forces.habit: we keep last month's split
forces.anxiety: what if the next-dollar numbers are too thin to trust

watch.metric: each channel's share of spend versus the agreed split
watch.source: ad platforms and brand brain (decision log)

drives.metric: blended cost per new customer, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 70 percent to Meta by habit. After: 55 percent, with Google search raised after it earned more per dollar.
jobs.not_for: a store with only 1 paid channel

jobs.job: When the weekly numbers land, flag top sellers where ad spend is up and stock is running out, so we stop paying for ads on items we cannot ship
jobs.circumstance: the best seller has 9 days of stock; its ads budget went up 20 percent

progress.functional: stock days next to ad spend for top items
progress.emotional: no more angry customers waiting for back orders
progress.social: get the ops lead and the buyer in step

jobs.hire_today: the founder or ops lead checking by hand, or nothing
jobs.fire: separate stock and ads reports

forces.push: ads spend on items that sell out
forces.pull: a weekly flag of the mismatch
forces.habit: ads and stock are different jobs
forces.anxiety: what if stock data lags

watch.metric: days of stock left on the top 10 sellers next to their ad spend, weekly

drives.metric: stockout days on top 10 sellers, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $4,000 spent on a sold-out item last month. After: ads paused 5 days before stockout.
jobs.not_for: a store with deep stock on every item

jobs.job: When I am away for a week, tell me only if something breaks, so I can switch off without fear
jobs.circumstance: the founder's first holiday in 2 years, checking the phone every hour on the beach

progress.functional: an alert only when a key number breaks its range, with who is on it
progress.emotional: rest without dread
progress.social: show the team I trust them to run the week

jobs.hire_today: phone checks every hour; a team member texting updates
jobs.fire: the hourly habit of checking sales

forces.push: the holiday is lost to worry
forces.pull: silence unless something breaks, and a named person already on it
forces.habit: check just in case
forces.anxiety: what if the alert misses the one thing that matters

jobs.little_hire: on any trip or day off

watch.metric: alerts sent while the founder is away, and founder logins while away

drives.metric: days from a break to a fix

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 30 phone checks a day on holiday. After: 1 alert all week, handled by the ops lead.
jobs.not_for: a founder with no team to act on an alert

jobs.job: When an agency or freelancer invoice arrives, match each line to work actually delivered, so I pay for what I got
jobs.circumstance: month start, the creative agency bills for 20 ads; the founder counts 12 live

progress.functional: each invoice line with its delivered work
progress.emotional: stop the feeling of being overcharged
progress.social: raise it with facts, not a quarrel

jobs.hire_today: the founder or bookkeeper checking by hand, or not at all
jobs.fire: paying on trust

forces.push: billed work that was never delivered
forces.pull: a line by line match with gaps flagged
forces.habit: paying is faster than checking
forces.anxiety: what if the vendor feels accused

watch.metric: invoice dollars with no matching delivered work, per month
watch.source: brand brain (vendor record) and accounting feed

drives.metric: vendor spend per dollar of gross profit, quarterly

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $2,400 a month billed for work not on file. After: 0 after 2 months.
jobs.not_for: a store with no outside vendors

jobs.job: When I review the agency's month, show the hours spent on each brand next to its fee, so I fix or drop the clients that lose us money
jobs.circumstance: agency owner, month end, the client that pays the least takes the most calls

progress.functional: hours and fee per brand, and the margin each leaves
progress.emotional: stop the feeling that some clients drain the team
progress.social: reprice or part ways with facts both sides can see

jobs.hire_today: a timesheet tool nobody reads against fees, and gut
jobs.fire: gut sense of which clients are hard

forces.push: unprofitable clients take the best people's time
forces.pull: margin per client each month, worst first
forces.habit: every client is a good client
forces.anxiety: what if the timesheets are wrong

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and before each contract renewal

watch.metric: hours booked per brand against the fee, monthly

drives.metric: agency margin per client, quarterly

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: 1 client runs at a 20 percent loss for the agency. After: repriced up 30 percent at renewal.
jobs.not_for: a founder running a single brand

jobs.job: When sales are up, tell me if the growth came from new buyers or from old ones, so I know whether we are growing or leaning on past customers
jobs.circumstance: quarter review, sales are up 15 percent, a partner is pleased, and nobody has checked that new customer orders fell 5 percent

progress.functional: new customer orders and returning customer orders, side by side, each week
progress.emotional: know the growth is real and will last
progress.social: tell a partner or an investor the true source of growth

jobs.hire_today: an analyst who builds it on request, or nothing, because the store's default reports blend the two
jobs.fire: one blended sales number as the headline

forces.push: a slowdown in new customers hides behind loyal buyers for months
forces.pull: new and returning shown apart, with the trend
forces.habit: total sales is the number everyone quotes
forces.anxiety: what if customer matching counts one buyer twice

jobs.little_hire: weekly, and at each quarter review

watch.metric: new customer orders and returning customer orders, weekly

drives.metric: new customers per month

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: sales up 15 percent while new customers fell 5 percent, unseen for 8 weeks. After: seen in week 2 and prospecting budget raised.
jobs.not_for: a store in its first 3 months, when almost every buyer is new

jobs.job: When booked sales look strong, show sales after returns, refunds and chargebacks next to them, so I know the growth is real
jobs.circumstance: a record month of $100,000 booked; the returns team says the bins are full

progress.functional: booked sales and kept sales on the same line
progress.emotional: no false comfort from a big number
progress.social: report numbers to a partner that will not shrink later

jobs.hire_today: the bookkeeper, monthly and after the fact
jobs.fire: booked sales as the headline number

forces.push: returns and disputes hide behind booked sales for weeks
forces.pull: both lines on one page each week, with the gap
forces.habit: booked sales is what the store dashboard shows first
forces.anxiety: what if returns land in a different week from the sale

watch.metric: sales after returns, refunds and chargebacks, weekly

drives.metric: return rate, 28 day

jobs.now_after: Example. Now: $100,000 booked, $78,000 kept, the gap seen at month end. After: both shown weekly, a sizing fault found in week 1.
jobs.not_for: a store with very few returns, such as food or consumables

jobs.job: When a month closes, tell me in pass or fail whether we made money on the average new customer, so I know if growth is safe to fund

jobs.little_hire: monthly, and before any big budget rise

drives.metric: contribution margin per new customer, 90 day

jobs.hire_today: nothing; most tools show 0 or a smaller total with no warning

forces.anxiety: what if so many fields go missing the report is useless

drives.metric: corrections sent after a report, per quarter
